hypotheses.justification: QuasiCompact f is only used to rewrite `f.ker.ideal U` to `RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom` by `Hom.ker_apply`. The statement is still true without it, and the proof can avoid that lemma. `f.ker` is `ofIdeals (fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom)`, so `f.ker.radical ≤ f.ker` follows from `le_ofIdeals_iff` (Galois connection, `I ≤ ofIdeals J ↔ I.ideal ≤ J`). It then suffices to show `(f.ker.ideal U).radical ≤ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom` for each affine open U. By `Hom.ideal_ker_le` (no QuasiCompact needed), `f.ker.ideal U ≤ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom`. The radical of that kernel is the kernel itself, because the kernel of a ring hom into the reduced ring Γ(X, f⁻¹U) is radical, which is exactly what `Ideal.isRadical_bot.comap` shows in the current proof. The reverse inequality `f.ker ≤ f.ker.radical` is `Scheme.IdealSheafData.le_radical`, and `radical_ideal` gives `radical.ideal U = (I.ideal U).radical`. I checked these in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Basic.lean. So the conclusion holds for any f with reduced source.
